IKIO.why: Trades below its IPO price. The only explanation found is a promotional blog citing foreign investor selling, earnings pressure and sector de-rating, which could not be confirmed. Working-capital strain from component shortages and redesigns was cited by management. Operations recovered in Q1 FY27: revenue up about 41% year on year to ₹169 crore, EBITDA margin 13.0% (9.4% a year ago).
IKIO.outlook: Management guided about 20-22% revenue growth for FY27 with margins close to FY26, and said Block II capacity was partly commercial in Q2 FY27. Risks flagged: component cost inflation, competition from Chinese electronics makers, and a heavy shift away from its older home-lighting contract business. The cause of the fall is not well documented.

IDEAFORGE.why: Defence drone maker with lumpy orders. The shares hit the 20% upper circuit in May 2026 after Q4 FY26: revenue about ₹141 crore, profit ₹60 crore, record FY26 order bookings of ₹530 crore, and about 86% of Q4 revenue from defence. It also approved a ₹500 crore QIP raise, completed in July 2026. Earlier quarters had losses (Q1 FY26 net loss ₹23.6 crore).
IDEAFORGE.outlook: IIFL upgraded to Buy with a ₹1,187 target on a stronger pipeline; JM Financial is Add with ₹905, warning that a ₹20,000 crore drone procurement programme may stretch over 18-24 months with awards slipping to FY28-29. The company is expanding into combat drones. Revenue swings with order timing.

NETWEB.why: Became an AI-infrastructure story. It launched NVIDIA-based AI supercomputers (Tyrone Camarero GB200 and Camarero Spark) in February 2026 and shares jumped 14%; AI systems are now its main revenue driver. June-quarter 2026 profit rose 180% to ₹85.23 crore. It raised ₹1,200 crore through a QIP in August 2026. The stock hit a record ₹5,241.65 on 19 June, corrected nearly 20%, then rebounded.
NETWEB.outlook: Order book was ₹2,098 crore in March 2026 plus ₹328 crore of L1 orders. One broker is Buy with a ₹5,698 target and another forecasts a 52% earnings CAGR over FY26-29. Risks: a very large run-up, sharp corrections and dependence on supply of NVIDIA hardware.

RISHABH.why: Q4 FY26 consolidated profit rose about 228% to ₹20 crore and the shares jumped 13% on the day to ₹528, with a ₹2 per share dividend. It is doubling its Nasik capacity and targets ₹100 crore from solar in 3-4 years, plus a European transformer order worth about ₹10 crore. The quarter's jump is off a low base.
RISHABH.outlook: Consolidated revenue growth was only about 1.3% in the period reviewed and its Lumel Alucast subsidiary saw revenue fall, so growth is thin. Third-party estimates (not company guidance) put revenue near ₹7.6-10.4 billion over FY26-28. At around 31x trailing earnings the valuation is not cheap.

ZAGGLE.why: Roughly flat against the IPO price after a steep drawdown: the stock traded between about ₹186 and ₹470 over the year to mid-2026, and was near ₹204-217 by May-August. No source explained the fall, and no regulator order against it was found in these searches.
ZAGGLE.outlook: No 2026 analyst outlook or management guidance turned up. Check the company's exchange filings and latest quarterly results for the reason behind the drawdown before relying on this entry.

YATRA.why: Below the IPO price. FY26 revenue rose to ₹1,007 crore from ₹795 crore, helped by the Globe Travels corporate-travel acquisition (₹128 crore, September 2024), but Q4 FY26 revenue fell 13.7% as the Middle East disruption hit international flights, hotels, packages and MICE. Earlier falls were put down to foreign investor selling and weak earnings across Indian equities.
YATRA.outlook: Medium-term targets are 20% annual growth in revenue less service cost and 30% in adjusted EBITDA, with recovery expected in H2 FY27. The company is also exploring restructuring alternatives, with timing uncertain. Sources disagreed on the FY26 net loss, so check the filing.

PROTEAN.why: Fell sharply in May 2025 when it said it was not considered for the next round of the Income Tax Department's PAN 2.0 project, having already more than halved from its August 2024 high of ₹2,225; Equirus cut it to Sell. Revenue for March 2026 was about ₹1,070 crore (₹910 crore a year earlier) and profit about ₹94 crore, roughly flat.
PROTEAN.outlook: Analysts forecast about 12.2% annual revenue growth and coverage is thin. New products include NPS Vatsalya, the Unified Pension Scheme and Bima Sugam. A new MD and CEO (Ajay Rajan) started on 1 June 2026. No FY27 guidance was found.

TATATECH.why: Fell by more than half to a March 2026 low of ₹507.50 on weak auto engineering demand (ramp-up delays and tariff uncertainty in North America), then recovered about 30% in six months to a high near ₹890 in August on Q1 FY27 profit growth and a Tenneco partnership expansion (more than $100 million of investment expected over 5 years). It depends heavily on Tata Motors and JLR.
TATATECH.outlook: Split views: Goldman Sachs is Sell with a ₹550 target (auto R&D shifting to software while it leans on body and mechanical work) and Elara is Sell at ₹490. Possible upside cited: scarce software deals among JLR's rivals, the VinFast account ramp-down ending, and aerospace growth.

RPTECH.why: Up about 2.7x. Drivers: strong enterprise PC demand (AI-enabled PCs up 129% in India, 25% of PC sales), price increases, and growth in Dell and semiconductor distribution. FY26 revenue rose about 14.9% to ₹15,827 crore. The shares hit a record ₹806 in 2026 after it agreed to buy control of VDA Infosolutions, a move into enterprise IT, data centres and cloud.
RPTECH.outlook: Margins are expected to hold at the top of a 2.5-3% EBITDA band; Dell contribution is expected to reach double digits in FY27. The brokerage warns higher prices could dent consumer demand in H2 FY27, and the share price has already run well above its ₹630 target. Q1 FY27 results were not found.
